title: Structural DWG checker and consumer write-policy boundary
mode: Primary-source web research and read-only local plan crosswalk; plan-only
scope: Screen a newly surfaced open-source DWG structural checker for a possible bounded, optional role in the existing writer evidence ladder.
Separate container integrity from object semantics, strict independent reading, and native CAD acceptance.
Cross-check LibreCAD_3 downstream DWG write policy without treating product policy as a codec capability result.
Preserve the fast per-slice validation cadence and prohibit imported or mutated peer fixture files from entering the repository.

sources.revision: Mutable main branch reviewed 2026-10-20; no immutable commit or release artifact pinned and no code executed
sources.observed: The README describes a pure-Python Tier 1 structural validator for AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032, based on ODA DWG specification chapter 4, checking header, page/section maps, data pages, checksums, decompression, required sections, and exact EOF. Tier 1 does not parse drawing objects. Its self-reported corruption table uses 22 LibreDWG test-data drawings and generated corruption variants. Optional Tier 2 invokes ODA File Converter with audit enabled and recovery disabled, then ezdxf.recover.readfile; it records converter errors and recovery/audit fixes. The README states audit can silently repair without a fix count, conversion output is nondeterministic, only macOS arm64 with ODA 27.9 was exercised, and Linux/Windows paths remain untested. The checker also documents unsupported versions, unprotected bytes, and missing object-level checks.

The document states DWG import is optional and read-only, its pinned libdxfrw claim ledger contains read-direction claims only with none promoted, and any future DWG writing requires promoted write claims, acceptance by an implementation LibreCAD does not control, and a project-level risk decision. This is product policy, not a measurement of the library writer.

The plan already requires a fast local loop and a separate composed external/native evidence checkpoint; the status document separates writer/callback routes from consumer capability and keeps support claims conservative. No local coverage conclusion was inferred solely from peer documentation.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-07 composed writer checkpoint: optional structural-only check for exact supported DWG targets
PAR-14 malformed-input test design: use corruption categories only where source audit finds a reachable uncovered boundary
Downstream consumer policy versus library writer evidence: maintain separate claims and ownership

planChanges: Classify dwg-verifier Tier 1 as a candidate optional structural check for exact AC1024/AC1027/AC1032 writer outputs; require an immutable source revision and output hash if used, and never count it as object-semantic or native acceptance evidence.

Exclude Tier 2 from strict/no-repair qualification because it uses ODA audit and ezdxf recovery, while its own documentation reports silent audit repairs, nondeterministic output, and untested Linux/Windows execution paths.
Use the peer corruption dimensions as a conditional source-audit checklist, not a new required campaign; generated mutations stay temporary and only use scratch-created or repository-owned seeds.
Separate downstream LibreCAD_3 product policy from libdxfrw writer capability and qualification.
limitations: The checker source page was mutable and not pinned to an immutable commit in this review; no release artifact was identified.
The checker's detection rates and corpus measurements are self-reported and were not independently reproduced.
Tier 1 covers only AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032 and does not parse objects or all CRC-covered structures.
Tier 2 depends on the ODA File Converter and ezdxf recovery and is not a strict independent semantic oracle.
No local production source was changed, no tests were run, and no external drawing or peer runtime was obtained.
